messages:
maria: FYI found a new advisory — CVE-2026-31415 in protobuf v4.23.1. unsafe deserialization when parsing user-supplied model artifacts. PoC circulating. tagging eng-security for prioritization.
alex: link? brief exploitability notes?
maria: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-31415 Exploitability: remote, requires a crafted artifact uploaded to our model-ingest endpoints. CVSS 8.2. Seems to allow arbitrary code execution during deserialization.
sam: This touches model-ingest (hosted) and private deployments that allow customer uploads. Hosted API: only customers who upload artifacts are at risk, not inference requests directly. Dedicated with BYO artifacts also exposed.
alex: SLA impact: low immediate user-facing latency risk, high security risk for customers who upload. If exploited could lead to data exposure — treat as high priority for customers in enterprise/tiered contracts.
jia: Recommend two-track response: 1) short-term mitigations (block unsigned artifacts, drop legacy parser flag, add strict content-type validation), 2) rolling patch to protobuf runtime ASAP. I can own the patch if we greenlight.
ops-lead: Can we do a targeted canary for model-ingest in staging/one-hosted-cluster first? Need rollback plan + 02:00-04:00 UTC maintenance window options from infra.
alex: Agree canary then staged rollout. For hosted: target 48h window for patch if mitigations applied now. For Dedicated/Private: notify customers and provide mitigations + scheduled patch (opt-in timeline) since many are air-gapped.
devsec-bot: Created detection rule: "suspicious-artifact-serialization" -> alert on unusual deserialization errors and exec attempts. Rule ID: DS-2026-31415.
maria: Proposed schedule: canary 2145012000 (tomorrow 02:00 UTC), 90m window; global hosted rollout 2145098400 (48h) with canary approval; send advisory to enterprise customers now with mitigation steps.
sam: Product note: for SLA/credits — if we need forced downtime for hosted patch, estimate affected requests <0.5% during window. ops-lead pls confirm region impact.
ops-lead: Confirmed: single-region canary first (us-west-2), staged to others. Will reserve 02:00-03:30 UTC slot and standby on-call. Backout: revert protobuf upgrade and fallback to strict-parser container image.
jia: Action items: (1) I’ll open PR with runtime patch + test vectors (assign to jia) (2) ops-lead schedule canary and page on-call (assign ops-lead) (3) devsec-bot will push detection rule and SIG alerts (4) alex to draft customer advisory for Dedicated/Private (assign alex).
alex: Draft advisory ready, will share for review in #product-security in 30m. Recommend labeling priority P1 for Dedicated enterprise customers, P2 for public hosted rollout due to lower exposure vector.
maria: Thanks. tagging @ops-lead @jia @alex — please update status in thread as tasks progress. :thumbsup:
ops-lead: Will update. will also add a temporary WAF rule to block suspicious artifact content-types as an additional short-term control.
devsec-bot: Note: added automated CI check to fail builds if protobuf <4.23.2 not used once PR merges.
jia: starting on patch PR now. ETA for initial build + unit tests: 6h.
alex: I'll send advisory and customer segmentation email after review. If any enterprise wants emergency support we should offer expedited private patch scheduling.
maria: putting this in incident-triage for tracking. will update thread when canary completes.
ops-lead: Canary started at 2145012000. monitoring logs now.
maria: received initial canary metrics — no regressions, no deserialization errors seen, waiting 30m for stability before staged rollout.
